text:
No. 24 Jennies to host Newman in home and MIAA soccer opener Sunday
J. D. Patino
The University of Central Missouri Jennies Soccer team will play its first home match of the season against Newman on Sunday, Sept. 20, at the South Recreation Complex in Warrensburg. The contest marks both the team's Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association (MIAA) and home opener for the 2026 season.
Sunday's game will be notable as the first official match played on Jennies Soccer's new artificial turf field, which was installed during the summer of 2026. The Jennies enter with a record of 5-1 overall after completing their first six matches on the road, including recent back-to-back 4-0 shutout victories over Harding and Ouachita Baptist.
Central Missouri's offense is led by senior midfielder Ryann Clark, sophomore midfielder Coryn Jespersen, sophomore forward Maryn Clement, and senior forwards Mikayla Ernst and Hadley Lockhart. Senior goalkeeper Kristen Wright has recorded five wins with a goals-against average of 0.19 through six matches. The team is currently third in conference scoring with 15 goals and second in goals allowed with just one goal conceded so far this season.
Sophomore Coryn Jespersen was named MIAA Women's Soccer Offensive Athlete of the Week for her performance from Sept. 7-13, contributing three assists in one match—a single-match record she now shares—and scoring a game-winning goal against Ouachita Baptist. Senior goalkeeper Kristen Wright previously earned MIAA Goalkeeper of the Week honors earlier this month.
The Jennies are ranked No. 24 nationally in the latest IWSOC/United Soccer Coaches Division II Top 25 Poll released on Tuesday, Sept. 15. At home since 2016 under head coach Lewis Theobald, Central Missouri has posted a record of 94-9-3 at South Recreation Complex and has remained undefeated at home five times during that span.
Head coach Lewis Theobald is entering his nineteenth year leading Central Missouri soccer and holds an all-time record of 324-58-31 at UCM—the most wins for any coach in program or conference history—and brought home a national championship title for UCM in 2017.
